citations.title: Federal Aviation Administration Issues Certification for Boeing 737 MAX-10 | Federal Aviation Administration
excerpts: Tuesday, October 20, 2026
**EVERETT, WA** — The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) today announced that following years of extensive review, the agency has issued the certification for Boeing’s 737 MAX-10.

The FAA issued an amended type certificate, which confirms the aircraft complies with all applicable design and safety requirements, and an updated Production Limitation Record, which authorizes aircraft production.

basis.reasoning: The FAA's dated announcement states that MAX 10 certification was issued and explains that the amended type certificate confirms design compliance while the production record authorizes production.

citations.title: Federal Register, Volume 91 Issue 194 (Thursday, October 8, 2026)
excerpts: ``` [Federal Register Volume 91, Number 194 (Thursday, October 8, 2026)] [Rules and Regulations] [Pages 64259-64267] From the Federal Register Online via the Government Publishing Office [ [www.gpo.gov](http://www.gpo.gov/) ] [FR Doc No: 2026-20680]

This material specifies procedures for replacing the LE outboard GRA with a LEOLA at leading edge slat 2 and slat 11 outboard locations and revising the operator's maintenance program to incorporate CMR document item 27-CMR- 14, ``Functionally check the Leading Edge Power Drive Unit Half System Torque Brake.'' This AD also requires Boeing Alert Requirements Bulletin B787- 81205-SB270051-00 RB, Issue 001, dated July 5, 2019, which the Director of the Federal Register approved for incorporation by reference as of October 11, 2019 (84 FR 54765, October 11, 2019).
This airworthiness directive (AD) is effective November 12, 2026.
The FAA is issuing this AD to address a potential condition in which the LE OB slat system could be out of position without flight deck annunciation.
The unsafe condition, if not addressed, could result in insufficient lift, resulting in inability to maintain continued safe flight and landing.

basis.reasoning: The October 8 final directive specifies hardware replacement and maintenance-program changes, identifies the unannunciated slat-position hazard and its safe-flight consequences, and gives the November 12 effective date. Its inclusion as investor-material is a judgment based on the safety implications.

citations.title: FAA: Boeing 737 Max 10 certification delayed by software issue
excerpts: Published Mon, Sep 28 2026 3:46 PM EDT Updated Mon, Sep 28 2026 4:16 PM EDT
The FAA said it won't certify Boeing's 737 Max 10 until it assesses a new software bug.
The issue, which Boeing flagged last month, could cut off automated landing guidance if pilots have to perform a go-around, or attempt a landing again.

Boeing said over the weekend that the issue could occur with a vertical navigation system after an aircraft misses an approach and has to go around and line up to land again, such as in situations when there is an obstruction on the runway, for example.

basis.reasoning: The dated report states that the FAA delayed certification pending assessment of a software bug and describes the navigation-guidance issue during a missed approach. It supports a certification pause, not a grounding.
